observations: Idle single user: 10 to 27 ms; unchanged by the optimisations.

Search at 1 user. Cycle 1: every search waited the 6 s rerank timeout (provider answers in 5-13 s). Now ~75 ms typical; p95 still shows the circuit breaker's cost (the first 3 searches and one 6 s probe every 30 s) on a sample of only 7-18 requests.

Chat at 1 user, 13 s typical (two model calls, about 3.2k input and 160 output tokens). Cycle 2's 35 s p95 was one slow provider call out of 3 samples and did not recur in Cycle 3. Token events arrive only after the model finishes, so time-to-first-token equals total time.
Mixed journey, 5 users: reads and search fine; chat p95 15 s and 100 % success. Fails the preset p95 only because of the search sample (rerank probe).
100 users, p95 100 ms to 60 ms.
250 users, p95 320 ms to 31 ms (plain-ASGI middleware).

Search, 100 users: throughput 13.6 to 46 req/s, p95 6.9 s to 4.1 s. 4.5 % of searches fell back to keyword-only ranking and missed the expected passage in the top 3: the embedding provider rate-limits above about 20 requests/s. Not seen in Cycle 1 only because the rerank wait capped throughput at 14 req/s.
Chat, 25 users: far above the provider's 40 calls/min. Cycle 1: 0 % success. Cycle 3: 52 % success, the rest waited out the 120 s run timeout in the queue.
Unique-query search, 100 users. Original code: 13.9 req/s, p95 6.9 s. Final: 51 req/s, p95 3.7 s, 3.6 % keyword-only fallbacks (embedding provider limit).
10 users, p95 17-27 ms.
50 users, p95 23-38 ms, about 50 req/s.

Search, 10 users: 1.4 req/s and 6.6 s p95 in Cycle 1; 9.4 req/s and 94 ms p95 in Cycle 3. Cycle 2 still failed this (6.1 s p95) because every concurrent request probed the reranker at once; Cycle 2b let a single search probe.
Search, 25 users: 3.5 to 23 req/s, p95 6.5 s to 100 ms.

Chat, 10 users. Cycle 1: 21 % success (provider 429s, amplified by retries). Now 100 % success; p95 60 s because calls queue behind the 36 calls/min limit (the provider allows 40). Capacity is about 18 chats/min.

Search with unique queries (cache cold), 10 users. Cycle 1b (original code): 6.5 s p95. Cycle 2b: 330 ms. Cycle 3: 5.3 s p95 because the reranker's latency sat just under its 6 s timeout, so the circuit kept closing and 10 concurrent searches waited on it; p50 stayed 77 ms.

Soak, 20 users mixed, 15 min in Cycle 3 (10 min in Cycle 1). Chat success 0 % (Cycle 1, provider window kept full by failing retries) to 97.8 %. API memory 484 to 515 MB over 15 min (about 2 MB/min, no plateau seen), file descriptors, threads and DB connections flat. 1.03 M input and 50.6 k output tokens consumed.
Spike 2 to 250 to 2 users: no errors, p95 770 ms to 60 ms.
Search spike 2 to 60 to 2: 100 % success; p95 7.1 s to 0.67 s.
Chat spike 2 to 30 to 2: success 5 % to 100 %; p95 66 s (queue).
Stress, 50 to 500 users. Cycle 1 knee at about 200 users (274 req/s, p95 560 ms, API CPU 100 %). Cycle 3 knee at about 300 users (494 req/s, p95 190 ms); at 500 users p95 790 ms with no errors.
Search stress: clean to 50 users (p95 100 ms); degrades at 100 (p95 1.8 s, 1.8 failures/s) and 150 users (p95 3.7 s); failures are keyword-only fallbacks from the embedding provider limit.
Chat stress: 5 users p95 15 s, 10 users 41 s, 60 users 68 s, success 92 %. Throughput is flat at the provider-bound 18 chats/min whatever the user count.
